title: Image Analysis Algorithm for Co-Migrated DNA Fragments in PFGE Profiles
author: Ibrahim El-khalil Adam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bthtnj6n

steps.title: Open PFGE image
steps.instruction: Navigate to the folder containing the PFGE image and open the image file in the analysis program.

steps.title: Set band/background polarity
steps.instruction: Tell the program whether DNA bands appear white on a black background or the opposite.

steps.title: Define lanes and bands
steps.instruction: Create lane definitions, then define each band within the lanes; perform manual modifications when the automatic detection is inaccurate.

steps.title: Assign ladder sizes
steps.instruction: Select the lane that contains the DNA ladder and assign each ladder band its size in kilobase‑pairs (kbp); multiply each kbp value by 1 000 to obtain the size in base pairs for calculations.

steps.title: Copy analysis data
steps.instruction: In GelAnalyzer2010a open the "Analysis info" window, press Ctrl + A to select all data, and copy it. The "Raw volumes" column corresponds to intensity profiles (pixel densities) for each band size (MW).

steps.title: Paste data into PAST
steps.instruction: Open PAST statistics, paste the copied data, and change the column attributes so that one column is labeled "Band size" and the other "Pixel density".

steps.title: Create preliminary polynomial fit
steps.instruction: Generate a polynomial fit of pixel density versus band size; record the initial coefficient of determination (R² ≈ 0.67113), which gives a rough estimate of co‑migrated fragments.

steps.title: Remove outlier values
steps.instruction: Identify values above the red reference line (odd pixel‑density values). Remove the corresponding band sizes and pixel densities for bands 2‑5, 10, and 15‑18 from both columns, then recreate the polynomial fit.

substeps.instruction: Note the final polynomial equation: EPD = -6.651E-11*BS^2 + 0.0013*BS + 191.2 (EPD = expected pixel density, BS = band size).

steps.title: Calculate expected pixel densities
steps.instruction: Open Microsoft Office™ Excel, paste the two columns (Band size and Pixel density), add an empty column, and apply the polynomial equation to each band size to compute expected pixel densities (EPD).

steps.title: Compare observed vs expected
steps.instruction: Compare observed pixel densities with the calculated EPDs; bands 1, 8, 9, and 11 show close agreement (single‑fragment bands), while band 2 has an observed value roughly twice the expected.

steps.title: Determine fragment count per band
steps.instruction: Create a column named "O/E" (observed/expected) by dividing each observed pixel density by its corresponding expected pixel density, then truncate the O/E values to obtain the fragment count per band (FCMs).
